hunks.baseline: In the silence of time brought to a halt, I slowly lifted my eyelids.
hunks.sol: In time brought to a standstill, amid a silence that seemed to last forever, I slowly opened my eyes.

hunks.baseline: My mind was hazy, as if shrouded in thick fog, yet my vision was clearer than ever.
hunks.sol: My mind was hazy, as though lost in thick fog, yet I could see more clearly than ever. Clearly enough to wonder if all of this was a dream.

hunks.baseline: Clear enough to make me wonder if all of this was a dream.
But the low voice that reached my ears a moment later was enough to remind me that this moment was no illusion.
hunks.sol: But the low voice that reached my ears a moment later reminded me that this was no illusion.

hunks.baseline: I raised my head and stared blankly at the old man.
hunks.sol: I looked up at the old man, dazed.

hunks.baseline: Then, recalling the formless qi that had flown across the space moments ago, cleaving it in two and missing me by no more than a thread, I parted my lips.
hunks.sol: I thought of the formless qi that had flown toward me, cleaving the space in two and missing me by no more than a thread’s width.

hunks.baseline: Everything felt natural.
The respectful way I had begun speaking, and the old man’s acceptance of my attitude as if it were only right.
hunks.sol: Everything felt natural. The respect that had crept into my voice, and the way the old man accepted it as if it were only right.

hunks.baseline: “A beam of light. A line.”
hunks.sol: “A ray of light. A line.”

hunks.baseline: “How could that be? It must have been formless.”
hunks.sol: “How could that be? It was formless.”

hunks.baseline: “You saw it, but didn’t see it. Then what was it?”
hunks.sol: “You saw it without seeing it? Then how did you see it?”

hunks.baseline: I suddenly found myself at a loss.
hunks.sol: I faltered.

hunks.baseline: Not because I didn’t know the answer to the old man’s question, but because the thought that had flashed through my mind as soon as I heard it seemed absurd even to me.
hunks.sol: Not because I didn’t know the answer, but because the thought that had flashed through my mind sounded absurd even to me.

hunks.baseline: But my silence was as good as an answer.
The old man’s gaze, whose depths I couldn’t begin to fathom, was already looking into my heart.
hunks.sol: My silence was as good as an answer, though. The old man’s unfathomable gaze was already looking into my heart.

hunks.baseline: “People often have the truth right before their eyes and still fail to believe it, passing it by. A truly regrettable thing.”
hunks.sol: “People often have the truth right before their eyes and still pass it by because they cannot believe it. What a pity.”

hunks.baseline: One step.
With that single stride, the old man erased all distance between us and whispered to me.
hunks.sol: One step was all it took for the old man to close the distance between us. He whispered:

hunks.baseline: “You saw what cannot be seen, and avoided what cannot be avoided. So why can’t you believe what you yourself did?”
hunks.sol: “You saw what cannot be seen, and dodged what could not be dodged. Why can’t you believe you did it?”

hunks.baseline: “Sit in meditation.”
hunks.sol: “Sit cross-legged.”

hunks.baseline: My mind was still hazy as if in a dream. I followed the old man’s words as if entranced and sat down.
hunks.sol: Still hazy as though in a dream, I sat as he instructed, almost without knowing what I was doing.

hunks.baseline: Then I heard his voice, no longer ringing in my ears but inside my head.
hunks.sol: Then I heard his voice again—not in my ears, but inside my head.

hunks.baseline: —Clear your mind like a stream. Keep your focus, and let yourself go with the flow.
hunks.sol: —Clear your mind like a stream. Hold your focus and let yourself follow the flow.

hunks.baseline: Suddenly, I felt as though I’d heard something like this said before, somewhere.
hunks.sol: A thought came to me. I’d heard something like this before, somewhere.

hunks.baseline: But the brief thought that crossed my mind vanished along with my consciousness as it sank deeper and deeper.
hunks.sol: But it was gone in an instant as my awareness sank deeper.

hunks.baseline: Light and darkness flickered endlessly before my eyes, throwing everything into confusion.
hunks.sol: Light and darkness flickered without end before my eyes, leaving me disoriented.

hunks.baseline: In that distant chaos, I forgot everything.
hunks.sol: Amid that overwhelming confusion, I forgot everything.

hunks.baseline: And yet the voice coming from somewhere was astonishingly clear.
hunks.sol: Yet the voice coming from somewhere remained astonishingly clear.

hunks.baseline: —Remember once more. What you saw. The sensation of that moment.
hunks.sol: —Remember what you saw. How it felt in that moment.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, I murmured in my mind the name of the thing that had no shape, color, or scent.
hunks.sol: Then I spoke the name of the thing with no shape, color, or scent in my mind.

hunks.baseline: It was everywhere and nowhere.
hunks.sol: Everywhere and nowhere.

hunks.baseline: That was right.
hunks.sol: Yes.

hunks.baseline: For a brief moment, I had seen its true nature clearly.
hunks.sol: For a brief moment, I had seen it clearly—through a new realm beyond the senses.

hunks.baseline: Through a new realm that lay beyond the senses.
And the owner of the voice echoing deep within my soul was no different from someone who had already set foot in that realm.
hunks.sol: And the owner of the voice echoing deep within my soul was someone who had already set foot in that realm.

hunks.baseline: Right.
I still hadn’t answered the old man’s earlier question.
hunks.sol: Right. I still hadn’t answered the old man’s question.

hunks.baseline: But this time, I could answer without hesitation.
I found the other eye hidden within me, the one even I hadn’t believed in.
hunks.sol: This time, though, I could answer without hesitation. That other eye hidden within me—the one even I hadn’t believed in—

hunks.baseline: At the moment those two words finally came to me and were branded into my mind—
hunks.sol: The moment those two words came to me and were branded into my mind—

hunks.baseline: —As always, you’ve made a good decision.
hunks.sol: —Good judgment, as always.

hunks.baseline: Along with the old man’s low voice, the light and darkness that had been endlessly clouding my vision scattered.
hunks.sol: At the sound of the old man’s low voice, the light and darkness that had kept flickering before my eyes scattered.

hunks.baseline: Or rather, everything surrounding me did.
hunks.sol: Or rather, everything around me did.

hunks.baseline: I exhaled the breath I’d been holding and looked around.
hunks.sol: I let out the breath I’d been holding and looked around.

hunks.baseline: Why was this happening?
hunks.sol: Why was this happening? How was it possible?

hunks.baseline: How could such a thing be possible?
Cracks spread in every direction like a pane of glass about to shatter, and the figure of the man standing beyond it twisted along with the shifting space.
hunks.sol: Cracks ran through it like glass about to shatter. Beyond them, the figure of the old man twisted along with the space.

hunks.baseline: In contrast to the unbelievable sight before me, the old man’s tone was calm and composed.
hunks.sol: His voice was calm, at odds with the impossible sight before me.

hunks.baseline: I stared at him as if entranced.
Then, recalling a fragment of a memory I’d long forgotten, I finally spoke.
hunks.sol: I stared at him. Then a piece of a memory I’d long forgotten came back to me.

hunks.baseline: The old man smiled faintly.
hunks.sol: The old man smiled.

hunks.baseline: It was neither a yes nor a no.
hunks.sol: Neither a yes nor a no.

hunks.baseline: But at last, I was certain.
Though the gray-white space and the old man looked different from how I remembered them, their essence hadn’t changed.
hunks.sol: But now I was certain. The gray-white space and the old man might look different from how they had then, but neither had changed at the heart of it.

hunks.baseline: And now I knew who the mysterious voice was that had sometimes come to me like an auditory hallucination since my Bone Transformation.
hunks.sol: I knew whose voice had come to me now and then like an auditory hallucination ever since my Bone Transformation.

hunks.baseline: With a voice I could barely force out, I stared at the old man, who only smiled in silence.
hunks.sol: I could barely force the word out as I looked at the old man smiling silently before me.

hunks.baseline: The one who had first taught me to circulate my qi when I’d just taken my first steps into the unknown world of Murim.
hunks.sol: The one who had first taught me to circulate my qi when I’d only just stepped into the unknown world of Murim.

hunks.baseline: The mysterious being I’d been forced to forget for so long because I’d thought he was just part of the tutorial system.
hunks.sol: The mysterious being I’d taken for part of the tutorial System, and forgotten for so long because of it.

hunks.baseline: “……Who on earth are you?”
hunks.sol: “…Who on earth are you?”

hunks.baseline: Was this what it felt like to be struck by lightning through the crown of your head?
hunks.sol: Was this what it felt like to have lightning strike the top of your head?

hunks.baseline: Faced with the immense truth at last, I trembled as the shock surged through me like a tidal wave.
hunks.sol: Faced at last with a truth this immense, I trembled as the shock washed over me like a tidal wave.

hunks.baseline: And at the same time, I knew instinctively:
The old man would never answer my question, and even this brief meeting was drawing to a close.
hunks.sol: At the same time, I knew it instinctively. The old man would never answer, and even this brief meeting was drawing to a close.

hunks.baseline: “You don’t have to answer. I already know.”
hunks.sol: “No need for me to answer. You already know that.”

hunks.baseline: Amid the contorting space, I shouted at the old man, whose face I could no longer make out.
hunks.sol: The space contorted. I could no longer make out the old man’s face, but I shouted toward him.

hunks.baseline: The old man’s voice sank low.
Then, cutting me off, he spoke.
hunks.sol: His voice dropped, cutting off the rest of my question.

hunks.baseline: “Well, it’s time to go. To the place where you belong.”
hunks.sol: “Now it’s time to go. To the place where you belong.”

hunks.baseline: The instant I opened my eyes wide, understanding what his words meant—
hunks.sol: My eyes widened as I understood what he meant.

hunks.baseline: As my vision was swept away, sucked toward somewhere, something glimmering touched my hand.
Along with the old man’s final words, ringing out like an auditory hallucination.
hunks.sol: The world in my sight rushed past as I was drawn away. Something glimmering touched my hand, and the old man’s final words rang through my head like a voice I was only imagining.

hunks.baseline: —Take it. It’s this old man’s final gift.
hunks.sol: —Take it. This is the last gift this old man can give you.

hunks.baseline: I instinctively clenched my hand around it.
hunks.sol: I grabbed it on instinct.

hunks.baseline: And as my consciousness faded, I heard a single sound ringing out from somewhere.
A clear bell chime I’d been certain I would never hear again.
hunks.sol: As my consciousness faded, I heard a sound from somewhere. A clear bell chime I’d been certain I would never hear again.

hunks.baseline: A brilliant light rushed from far away and covered my vision.
hunks.sol: A brilliant light came rushing from far away and filled my vision.

hunks.baseline: The old man left alone gazed in silence at the empty space for a long while.
hunks.sol: Left alone, the old man gazed in silence at the empty place for a long while.

hunks.baseline: The person who had just disappeared must have seen the entire gray-white space vanish, but the old man knew better.
hunks.sol: To the person who had just vanished, it must have looked as though the entire gray-white space was disappearing. But the old man knew better.

hunks.baseline: This space would last forever, and Jin Taekyung had been no more than a guest who’d stopped by for a brief visit.
hunks.sol: This space would last forever. Jin Taekyung had only been a guest passing through.

hunks.baseline: And he himself would once again have to continue his endless, uncertain wait.
hunks.sol: And the old man would once again have to wait, with no telling when that wait might end.

hunks.baseline: “When will it end?”
hunks.sol: “When will I be able to finish this?”

hunks.baseline: The old man murmured softly.
He had spent so long alone that talking to himself had become a habit.
hunks.sol: He murmured to himself. After so long alone, talking to himself had become a habit.

hunks.baseline: With a bitter smile on his wrinkled lips, the old man looked around.
hunks.sol: A bitter smile touched his wrinkled lips as he looked around.

hunks.baseline: An endless gray-white space stretching in every direction.
Cold and pale, it was the old man’s only home—and a vast prison without bars or an exit.
hunks.sol: Gray-white space stretched endlessly in every direction. Cold and pale, it was his only home—and a vast prison with neither bars nor an exit.

hunks.baseline: But the brief emptiness brought on by that truth soon passed, and the old man’s eyes settled back into calm.
hunks.sol: The emptiness that thought brought lasted only a moment. His gaze soon grew calm again.

hunks.baseline: He was a prisoner in this prison by his own choice, not because anyone else had forced him.
hunks.sol: After all, no one had forced him to become a prisoner here. He had chosen it himself.

hunks.baseline: “Yes. So that’s enough.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. That’s enough.”

hunks.baseline: The old man muttered quietly, as if making a promise to himself, and began to walk.
hunks.sol: He murmured the words as though renewing a promise to himself, then started walking.

hunks.baseline: Then, suddenly, he stopped and turned to look back along the way he’d come.
hunks.sol: A moment later, he stopped and turned to look back along the path he had taken.

hunks.baseline: Or, more precisely, at the place where the guest who had visited after so long had stayed.
hunks.sol: No—at the place where his first visitor in so long had stood.

hunks.baseline: Letting the name slip from his lips, the old man wondered:
Could he really do it?
Had his choice truly been right?
hunks.sol: The name left his lips, and he wondered if Taekyung could do it. If the choice he had made had truly been the right one.

hunks.baseline: And if he’d made the wrong choice, how terrible and cruel would the future ahead be?
hunks.sol: And if he was wrong, what terrible, cruel future awaited them?

hunks.baseline: But all those worries were meaningless.
The old man had already made his choice, and thanks to his help, Jin Taekyung had been given another chance.
hunks.sol: But there was no point dwelling on it. He had already made his choice, and with his help, Jin Taekyung had been given another chance.

hunks.baseline: “I suppose I have no choice but to believe in you.”
hunks.sol: “I suppose I’ll have to put my faith in you.”

hunks.baseline: With words that would never reach him, the old man resumed his halted steps.
Then he began to walk slowly.
Across the endless gray-white space, just as he always had.
hunks.sol: The words would never reach Taekyung. The old man began walking again, slowly crossing the endless gray-white space as he always had.

hunks.baseline: Clutching his Disciple’s lifeless body, he sobbed quietly, oblivious to everything around him.
hunks.sol: He held his Disciple’s lifeless body and sobbed quietly. Nothing around him mattered anymore—not the shouts and clash of steel that still rang out, nor the people watching him.

hunks.baseline: The cheers and clangor of steel that continued to ring out even now. The gazes of those watching him.
None of it mattered to the Master who had lost his one and only Disciple.
hunks.sol: The Master who had lost his only Disciple did not hold back his tears.

hunks.baseline: He didn’t hold back his tears.
No—he couldn’t.
hunks.sol: He couldn’t.

hunks.baseline: Only two years out of a life that had lasted over a hundred, but his time with Jin Taekyung had shone brighter than any other.
hunks.sol: Only two years out of a life that had lasted more than a hundred. Yet his time with Jin Taekyung had shone brighter than any other.

hunks.baseline: And now that Jin Taekyung, his Disciple, was dead.
hunks.sol: And now Jin Taekyung—his Disciple—was dead.

hunks.baseline: He had left for a faraway place, despite his Master’s plea for him to live.
hunks.sol: Despite his Master’s plea for him to live, he had gone somewhere far away.

hunks.baseline: That final voice wouldn’t leave his ears.
hunks.sol: Those last words would not leave Jeok Cheongang’s ears.

hunks.baseline: The corners of Taekyung’s mouth, strained into a smile for the sake of his grieving Master. His eyes, half-closed and empty. Even now, they seared into Jeok Cheongang’s heart like a brand.
hunks.sol: The corners of Taekyung’s mouth, raised with effort into a smile for his grieving Master. His half-closed, empty eyes. Even now, the sight seared into Jeok Cheongang’s heart like a brand.

hunks.baseline: He was swallowed by grief so profound he couldn’t make sense of anything.
His eyes blurred by tears that kept welling up, he couldn’t see what he needed to see.
hunks.sol: Grief overwhelmed him until he could make sense of nothing. Tears kept filling his eyes, hiding what he needed to see.

hunks.baseline: At the moment one tear rolled down the Master’s cheek and touched his dead Disciple’s hand—
hunks.sol: A tear rolled down the Master’s cheek and fell onto his dead Disciple’s hand.

hunks.baseline: The surface of the blood rippled with a sudden tremor, and the finger submerged in it moved.
hunks.sol: The surface of the blood trembled. A finger submerged in it moved.
